subject: Study Skills
title: Lecture 11 – Test Preparation and Taking Skills

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What is the key to success and high scores on tests?
A.explain: Good preparation for tests is the key for success and high scores. Having more knowledge than you think does not guarantee doing well without good preparation.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which question type is used in the SCFHS SLE?
A.explain: MCQs is the type of questions used in SCFHS SLE. Short-answer questions, clinical case scenarios, and stem and lead-in are parts or other types of questions.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What is the main reason capable students are not successful?
A.explain: The main reason capable students are not successful is exam stress and anxiety. Poor preparation, peer competition, and lack of sleep are causes of stress, not the main reason for failure itself.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which factors cause exam stress and lead to anxiety and panic?
A.explain: Causes of stress include poor preparation, negative thoughts and fear of failing, peer competition, and not enough sleep the night before. Thinking positively and joining a study group are preparation strategies.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What happens when you panic?
A.explain: When you panic, your memory is inhibited, your ability to focus decreases, and you become easily confused. The other options are test-taking or preparation strategies.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What is the key to deal with exam stress, anxiety, and panic?
A.explain: The key to deal with exam stress, anxiety, and panic is good preparation. Scanning the test is a test-taking tip, while wild guessing and peer competition are not solutions.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which actions are recommended to 'Study Well'?
A.explain: Studying well includes attending all classes, reviewing notes, checking handouts and summaries, answering as much questions as you can, linking with teachers, and joining a study group. Skipping tough ones is a test-taking strategy.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What should you do the day and night before the test?
A.explain: The day and night before the test, you should think positively, review notes, review easily forgotten info, sleep early and sleep well, and prepare stationery. Waking up early and working out are for the day of the test.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Why is a good breakfast recommended on the day of the test?
A.explain: Having a good breakfast is recommended because it is your brain's fuel for the exam. Working out helps you relax, underlining fixes attention, and certainty marking tracks revisits.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Who should you avoid being around on the day of the test?
A.explain: On the day of the test, don't be around pessimistic or anxious colleagues. Teachers, lab assistants, and study groups are not mentioned as people to avoid.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: A student follows the 5-day test preparation plan in reverse order.

steps.prompt: What is the main task for Day 5?
After reading and highlighting on Day 5, what is the main task for Day 4?
After using mnemonics on Day 4, what is the main task for Day 3?
After rewriting briefly on Day 3, what is the main task for Day 2?
After answering questions on Day 2, what is the main task for Day 1?
After reviewing notes on Day 1, what do you go over just before the test?

A.explain: Day 5: read and highlight. Day 4: mnemonics. Day 3: rewrite briefly. Day 2: answer questions. Day 1: review notes and go over difficult information just before the test.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: A student applies general test taking tips 1 through 7 during a paper exam.

steps.prompt: Tip 1: what do you do with the instructions?
After reading instructions carefully, why scan the whole paper test (Tip 2)?
After scanning to budget time, what does Tip 4 advise when you can answer instantly?
After answering instantly, how do you handle a tough question on paper (Tip 5)?
After skipping tough questions, what does certainty marking (Tip 6) do?
After tracking what needs review, what is the rule if you run out of time (Tip 7)?
After deciding never to leave blanks, what does Tip 3 advise overall?

A.explain: Tip 1 read instructions. Tip 2 scan to budget time per question. Tip 3 budget your time. Tip 4 answer instantly and move on. Tip 5 skip tough ones until easier questions done. Tip 6 certainty marking tracks revisits. Tip 7 never leave blanks.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: A student applies general test taking tips 8 through 14 to analyze question features.

steps.prompt: What does Tip 8 say to do before answering?
After understanding the question, why underline key data (Tip 9)?
After underlining to fix attention, what do qualifying words do (Tip 10)?
After noticing qualifying words alter the statement, what do negative prefixes do (Tip 11)?
After reversing meaning with prefixes, what does a double negative mean (Tip 12)?
After understanding double negatives, what to read first in a graph question (Tip 13)?
After reading the title and axes, why plan to finish early (Tip 14)?

A.explain: Tip 8: Understand the question first. Tip 9: Underline to fix attention. Tip 10: Qualifying words alter statements. Tip 11: Negative prefixes reverse meaning. Tip 12: Double negatives mean positive. Tip 13: Read graph title and axes first. Tip 14: Finish early for review time.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What characterizes Simple (Recall) MCQs?
A.explain: Simple (Recall) MCQs ask about knowledge recall or recognition and are direct questions. Cognitive MCQs require higher functions, are indirect, and are based on case scenarios.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Cognitive MCQs are based on what?
A.explain: Cognitive MCQs require higher cognitive functions and are based on a case scenario (a clinical case) or a problem that needs solving. Simple recall and direct questions describe Simple MCQs.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Match MCQ structure parts to their definitions.
A.explain: The stem is the clinical case scenario. The lead-in is the question asked. The options are the 4 choices including the correct answer.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: A student chooses between 'above down' and 'down up' approaches for an MCQ.

steps.prompt: When use the 'Above down' approach?
After deciding to use 'Above down' because you prepared well, what is the first step?
After reading the stem in 'Above down', what do you underline in it?
After underlining key data, when do you figure out the correct answer?
After figuring out the answer, when is the 'Down up' approach recommended instead?
When the stem is complex and you use 'Down up', what to read first?

A.explain: 'Above down' is used when prepared well, starting with the stem, underlining key data, and figuring out the answer before seeing options. 'Down up' is used for complex stems, starting with the lead-in and options.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: According to MCQ Tip 3, when change an answer?
A.explain: MCQ Tip 3 advises not to second guess yourself. Only change answers if you are absolutely sure the current answer is incorrect.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What does Tip 4 for answering MCQs advise to avoid?
A.explain: MCQ Tip 4 advises to avoid patterns and avoid middle dumping. Reading options, eliminating choices, and deciding beforehand are other recommended tips.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What defines 'Educated guessing'?
A.explain: Educated guessing is made using judgment and a particular level of knowledge and is therefore more likely to be correct. Wild guessing is based on no knowledge.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What defines 'Wild guessing'?
A.explain: Wild guessing is made based on no knowledge or information. Educated guessing uses judgment and knowledge.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What do Short Answer Questions (SAQs) test?
A.explain: SAQs require the examinee to provide information, not to choose it. They test the examinees' ability to synthesize or create (write) the answer.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which are recommended tips for answering SAQs?
A.explain: SAQ tips include formulating first, clear handwriting, being focused, using technical language, and following order. You should not underestimate the examiner or leave answers blank.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: According to SAQ Tip 5, what if order matters?
A.explain: SAQ Tip 5 states that if order matters, then follow it.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Match computerized test strategies to their actions.
A.explain: A positive goal shows intention to do well. Understand software commands to use the interface. Do not rush if feedback is incorrect. Use relaxation if tensing up.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What to do before leaving a computerized test?
A.explain: Before leaving the test, jot down (highlight) any questions that concerned or confused you.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What should you prepare the night before?
A.explain: The night before the test, prepare your stationery for the exam along with sleeping early and reviewing notes.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What does Tip 6 ('Certainty marking') do?
A.explain: Certainty marking helps you keep track of what needs to get answered or revisited.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which word is a 'Qualifying Word'?
A.explain: Qualifying words include Always, Never, Except, Only, and others that alter the statement's meaning. Stem, lead-in, and options are parts of an MCQ.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What do negative prefixes do to meaning?
A.explain: Negative words and prefixes change the meaning to the opposite.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: In an MCQ, what is the 'Lead-in'?
A.explain: The Lead-in is a question, like: Which of the following is...?

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What to do before reading MCQ options (Tip 5)?
A.explain: MCQ Tip 5 advises trying to decide the answer before reading the options.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What to eliminate at first glance (MCQ Tip 2)?
A.explain: MCQ Tip 2 advises eliminating choices you know are incorrect at 1st glance.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: According to SAQ Tip 6, what not to do?
A.explain: SAQ Tip 6 states: Don't underestimate the examiner.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What keeps a focused mind on computer tests?
A.explain: Use concentration strategies to keep a focused mind and deal with distractors during computerized tests.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: On the day of the test, why do some workout?
A.explain: Doing some workout on the day of the test helps you relax. Breakfast is brain fuel, underlining fixes attention, and certainty marking tracks revisits.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: If you don't know the answer to a question, what should you do?
A.explain: Your goal is to collect marks. Don't leave any question unanswered. If you don't know the answer, guess it.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Match each MCQ strategy to its action.
A.explain: Read all options before selecting. Eliminate incorrect ones instantly. Avoid second guessing by changing only if sure. Avoid patterns like middle dumping. Decide the answer before reading options.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Match each SAQ strategy to its action.
A.explain: Formulate the answer before writing. Use clear handwriting to make it legible. Be focused and get straight to the point. Use technical terminology. Follow the sequence if order matters. Respect the examiner by not underestimating them.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: If instructions are spoken by invigilators, what should you do?
A.explain: Tip 1 states to read instructions carefully, and if spoken by invigilators, listen attentively to them.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What should you do when you see a qualifying word?
A.explain: When you see a qualifying word, circle it to fix attention on it. Crossing out is for double negatives, and underlining is for key data.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which are common negative prefixes or words?
A.explain: Common negative prefixes and words include un, non, dis, and not. 'Except' is a qualifying word, and 'false' is a true/false qualifier, not a prefix.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Cognitive MCQs are based on which items?
A.explain: Cognitive MCQs are based on a case scenario (a clinical case) or a problem that needs solving (Math or Physics problem). The other options describe Simple MCQs or SAQs.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which conditions favor the 'above down' approach?
A.explain: The 'above down' approach is used when you have time, prepared well, and the stem is simple and easily readable. The other conditions favor the 'down up' approach.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which conditions favor the 'down up' approach?
A.explain: The 'down up' approach is used when you don't have time, did not prepare well, the stem is complex, or you are not good at English. Having time and preparing well favor 'above down'.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which describe Short Answer Questions (SAQs)?
A.explain: SAQs require the examinee to provide information and test the ability to synthesize or create the answer. The other options describe Simple or Cognitive MCQs.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which are essential strategies for computerized tests?
A.explain: Essential strategies include using multiple-choice strategies, not answering too quickly, and discussing skills with the lab assistant or instructor. Skipping, leaving blank, and second guessing are not recommended.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: According to the conclusion, test preparation prevents what?
A.explain: Test preparation makes test taking easy and prevents test anxiety and panic.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Tips for which test types are important for any test taker?
A.explain: Tips for taking MCQs and SAQs tests are important for any test taker.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Test taking skills are important for whom?
A.explain: Test taking skills are important for everyone in education.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which actions belong to the day of the test?
A.explain: Day of the test actions include waking up early, working out, having breakfast, attending early, and quick review. Sleeping early and preparing stationery belong to the night before.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which actions belong to the day and night before the test?
A.explain: Day and night before actions include thinking positively, reviewing notes, reviewing easily forgotten info, sleeping early, and preparing stationery. Waking up early and working out are for the day of the test.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Without good preparation, what happens even if you have more knowledge than you think?
A.explain: You most probably have more knowledge than what you think you do. But, without good preparation you will not do well on tests. The other options are results of panic.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: What is a key constraint for online exams regarding skipping questions?
A.explain: In an online exam, there is no back to previous question, unlike a paper exam where you can skip tough ones and return to them later.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which words from the first group are listed as 'Qualifying Words'?
A.explain: Qualifying words include Always, Never, Including, All, Because, and Must. Stem and Lead-in are parts of an MCQ structure.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which words from the second group are listed as 'Qualifying Words'?
A.explain: Qualifying words include Weak, Strong, Positive, Negative, Except, and More than. Options and Cues are parts of test structures.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which words from the third group are listed as 'Qualifying Words'?
A.explain: Qualifying words include Less than, True, False, Superior, Inferior, and Few. Summary and Record are note-taking terms.

A.cat: Lecture 11 - Test Preparation and Taking Skills
A.q: Which words from the fourth group are listed as 'Qualifying Words'?
A.explain: Qualifying words include Only and Absolutely, along with others like Always, Never, Except, and All. Main notes and Recall are Cornell note-taking terms.
